 Live Updates Updated Fri, Oct 30 2026 1:14 PM EDT Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Nasdaq plunges 3%, heads for worst day since June as tech stocks lead sell-off: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Justina Lee Deena Zaidi Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange at the opening bell in the Financial District of New York City. Angela Weiss | Afp | Getty Images The Nasdaq Composite tumbled on Friday, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed as traders moved out of key stocks related to artificial intelligence and into more defensive areas of the market.
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq lost 3% and was on track for its worst single-day performance since June. The blue-chip Dow was down 483 points, or 0.9%, while the S&P 500 slid 1.9%.
 Amazon shares lost 2% after the company reported earnings and revenue for the third quarter that fell short of Wall Street's expectations . The company also posted negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion and maintained its 2026 capital expenditures forecast for $220 billion.
 Intel , meanwhile, slide 29% after issuing a weak outlook for the current quarter, pointing to a slowdown in PCs. Revenue in the company's client computing and physical artificial intelligence group declined 5% from the year-ago quarter to $8.1 billion.
 Sandisk was also down 12%, even as its fiscal first quarter results beat estimates. The data storage company announced an eight-for-one forward stock split.
 Chipmakers more broadly were under pressure as well. Advanced Micro Devices dropped 11%, while others such as Nvidia and Broadcom fell 4% and 5%, respectively.
 As investors rotated out of tech, defensive areas such as consumer staples and healthcare saw gains. Walmart and Coca-Cola each rose nearly 2%, while Procter & Gamble climbed more than 1%, supporting the Dow. Fellow Dow members Merck and Amgen added around 2%.
 "The tone has changed a bit, and whether that changes the sustainability of the rotation is still yet to be determined," said Globalt's Keith Buchanan, who noted that this is a "scrutinizing" and "discerning" market. "Last year was hope. This year is: At the end of day, how does this all work in real world terms, like how to finance [it] and who gets the economics. Those questions are much more difficult to answer."
 "There are real economy risks, and the market's picking up on that," the senior portfolio manager added.
 Adding to the downbeat sentiment, The Financial Times reported, citing sources, that Blackstone told investors Anthropic may not receive an investment-grade rating after its debut. Anthropic's S-1 filing offered some momentum to the AI trade earlier this week, but pressure resumed as Wall Street digested more tech earnings.
 On Thursday, Alphabet shares posted their worst day on record after the company missed on earnings and revenue in the third quarter and posted negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion. The Google-parent's slide dragged the Nasdaq to a more than 1% loss in the regular session.
 Friday marks the final trading day in October. The month has been rocky for the AI trade, with investors paying close attention to companies' spending around the build-out. Hyperscalers Alphabet and Microsoft haven't lifted their capital expenditures forecasts .
 At the same time, neoclouds — the cloud-computing companies that are behind the infrastructure needed for AI datacenters — are facing investor scrutiny over their debt levels . CoreWeave , which has seen a surge in its bond yields, is the poster child of that worry: Shares have cratered more than 37% in October. Nebius is heading for a 33% decline on the month.
 The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) , which includes AI memory plays Micron and Seagate Technology, is off 20% in October, while the iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI ) is down 17%.
 As traders prepare to wrap up the month, the Nasdaq Composite is heading for a 5% fall. The S&P 500 is on track for a decline of less than 1%, while the Dow is on pace to rise 2%.
 18 Min Ago Stocks making big moves: Nvidia, Micron Technology, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
 Cheng Xin | Getty Images Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading: 
 Semiconductor stocks — Chipmakers suffered Friday as technology stocks sold off and concern reemerged about the strength of the artificial intelligence trade. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) slumped 7%, Astera Labs tumbled 12%, Qualcomm dropped 11% and Nvidia lost 4%.
 AI infrastructure plays — The iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) slumped more than 7%, Micron Technology slid more than 5%, Lumentum Holdings by more than 10% and Arista Networks by almost 8%, as stocks tied to the artificial intelligence buildout continued to lose air. CNBC's David Faber also said Friday that the proposed deal for Lumentum by Marvell Technology won't come at a big premium.
 Regeneron Pharmaceuticals – The biotech company jumped 11%. Third-quarter results beat estimates, with Regeneron earning $20.07, excluding items, on revenue of $5.12 billion. The FactSet consensus sought $16.42 per share and $4.56 billion. For the full-year period, Regeneron is calling for non-GAAP gross margin on net product sales of about 86%, up from its earlier guidance of 84% to 85%.
 Read the full list here .
 — Ananya Chetia 
 1 Hour Ago Marvell's potential acquisition of Lumentum may not have that large of a premium, CNBC's David Faber reports
 Marvell Technology 's possible takeover of Lumentum is anticipated to be an all-stock deal with not that large of a premium, according to CNBC's David Faber.
 A deal might be announced as soon as next week, Faber also said.
 Shares of Lumentum were down around 10% in midday trading Friday. Marvell shares fell more than 9%.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon LITE, 1-day — Sean Conlon 
 2 Hours Ago Analysts say buy the dip on Amazon
 A worker unloads Amazon packages from a Prime delivery truck in New York, US, on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Wall Street analysts are still bullish on Amazon after the company's third-quarter results disappointed investors.
 Analysts said investors should look past the results and massive spending and instead focus on signs that its corporate strategy is already beginning to pay off. 
 "Growth was disappointing vs expectations … but this seems mostly an expectations miss as $3.8bn added [quarter over quarter] was the second highest … added in AWS history and it does not change AWS's potential for further acceleration and its long-term opportunity," Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak said Friday in a note to clients.
 Shares were last down 1%.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon AMZN, 1-day CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here .
 — Liz Napolitano 
 3 Hours Ago Consumer staples and healthcare sectors gain Friday as tech falls
 A shopper browses a holiday food display while shopping for groceries ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday at an Albertsons supermarket in Redmond, Washington, U.S., November 24, 2025. David Ryder | Reuters Defensive sectors, including consumer staples and healthcare are moving higher on Friday amid weakness in the tech sector that has the Nasdaq down more than 2%.
 State Street's Consumer Staples Select Sector ETF (XLP) gained nearly 2%, hitting a new intraday all-time high to $90 with several stocks in the category reaching 52-week highs.
 Shares of tobacco product company Altria Group popped more than 2%, reaching a 52-week high of $79.
 Consumer goods company Philip Morris rose 1.6%, reaching a 52-week high of $214 per share.
 Keurig Dr. Pepper rose 1.4% to a 52-week high of $36. 
 Meanwhile, State Street's Health Care Select Sector ETF (XLV) gained 1.5$, reaching a 52-week high of $187.
 The fund's top holdings including Eli Lilly , Johnson & Johnson , Pfizer , and Gilead all rising Friday with each stock reaching 52-week highs. 
 Regeneron particularly stands out after the pharma company reported a strong third quarter print Friday morning that sent it stock soaring more than 12%.
 — Paulina Likos 
 4 Hours Ago Gold, silver fall to lowest levels since November 2025
 Argor-Heraeus' CEO Robin Kolvenbach holds one kilo bars of silver and gold at the plant of refiner and bar manufacturer Argor-Heraeus in Mendrisio, Switzerland, July 13, 2022. Denis Balibouse | Reuters Gold and silver prices reached their lowest levels in almost a year on Friday.
 Gold futures dropped to a low of $3,946. That's the lowest level since Nov. 5, 2025, when gold traded as low as $3,935.70.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Gold futures, 1-year Silver futures hit a low of $49.66, the lowest level since Nov. 24, 2025, when they traded as low as $49.37.
 — Gina Francolla and Sean Conlon 
 4 Hours Ago Stocks open lower
 The three major averages began Friday's session in the red.
 The Nasdaq Composite declined 2.2% just after the opening bell, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 155 points, or 0.3%. The S&P 500 lost 1.2%
 — Sean Conlon 
 5 Hours Ago 2-year yield on pace to close below 50-day moving average for first time since August
 The 2-year Treasury note yield fell on Friday , dropping below the 50-day moving average level of 4.609%.
 The move puts the yield on track to close below that key level for the first time since Aug. 18.
 The yield had dipped below the level briefly on Thursday on an intraday basis.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon US2Y, 3-month — Gina Francolla and Sean Conlon 
 5 Hours Ago Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: Intel, Amazon, Reddit, Chevron & more
 An Amazon Delivery sign is pictured on the upper exterior facade of an office building in West Jordan, Utah, United States, on August 29, 2026. Charles-McClintock Wilson | Nurphoto | Getty Images Check out the companies making the biggest moves premarket: 
 Intel —Shares tumbled 23% after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance for the fourth quarter . The company sees fourth-quarter earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue ranging between $15 billion and $16 billion. That's below LSEG estimates of 43 cents in earnings per share and revenue of $17.1 billion. 
 Rivian Automotive — The electric vehicle maker jumped over 8% after it reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. Rivian lost an adjusted 48 cents per share on revenue of $2.16 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a loss of 62 cents per share on revenue of $1.99 billion. The company also increased its guidance on deliveries .
 Amazon —Shares slipped nearly 6% in the premarket after the e-commerce giant reported third-quarter results that missed analyst expectations. The company also posted negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion .
 Read the full list here .
 — Ananya Chetia 
 6 Hours Ago Oil prices rise, head for monthly gain
 Oil prices rose on Friday, pacing for yet another month of gains.
 U.S.  West Texas ⁠Intermediate ‌crude futures advanced 2% to $104.04 per barrel, while Brent crude futures added 2.3% to $117.50 a barrel.
 The latest move higher puts WTI's month-to-date climb at roughly 15%, while Brent has risen more than 13% on the month.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon WTI, month-to-date — Sean Conlon 
 8 Hours Ago European natural gas prices surge past 100 euros, fueling winter price risk fears
 Marianvejcik | Istock | Getty Images Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF) futures for December delivery rose 3.77% to 101.63 euros ($113) per megawatt-hour on Friday, the highest level since late 2022, putting Europe's benchmark gas contract up 35.75% for the month, according to Trading Economics data.
 BlackRock said Europe looks "particularly vulnerable" to a colder winter, with natural gas storage now at around 75% — its lowest seasonal level since recordkeeping began in 2011.
 "A colder winter could push European energy prices, already up 170% this year, higher," BlackRock analysts said in an Oct. 27 note. 
 — Hugh Leask 
 9 Hours Ago European shares fall as tech stocks join global sell-off
 European shares were broadly lower in early trading on Friday, dragged lower by the tech sector. 
 Shortly after the opening bell, the pan-European Stoxx 600 was down by 0.3%. The Stoxx 600 Technology index fell 1.9% as tech stocks joined a global rout on the back of disappointing earnings from U.S. tech giants Amazon and Intel. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 10 Hours Ago AstraZeneca beats expectations, sees pipeline generating $20 billion in 2027
 AstraZeneca Plc signage at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Friday, June 5, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images AstraZeneca beat market expectations with quarterly results published Friday, as Britain's largest drugmaker reaffirmed its full-year and medium-term sales targets, citing a rich pipeline. 
 Third-quarter revenue grew 7% at constant exchange rates and came in at $16.2 billion, ahead of FactSet estimates of $16 billion. Core earnings per share were $2.79, and beating expectations of $2.59, up 19% year-on-year.
 The beat was driven by double-digit growth in its oncology, respiratory & immunology, and rare diseases businesses, offsetting declining sales from loss of exclusivity for its heart drug Farxiga, AstraZeneca said as it touted its drug candidates yet to hit the market. 
 "Our rich series of upcoming readouts in 2027 has a potential of more than twenty billion dollars," CEO Pascal Soriot said in a statement. 
 In 2026, AstraZeneca expects to grow revenue by mid-to-high single digits and core profits by low double digits. 
 Analysts largely expect the drugmaker to hit its stated goal of generating $80 billion in sales by 2030, despite a July clinical trial flop that would reduce those margins. 
 — Elsa Ohlen 
 10 Hours Ago Japan's Nikkei falls 2.1%, South Korea's Kospi declines 3.5%
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  closed 2.12% lower at 63,290.11, while South Korea's Kospi fell 3.48% to 5,730.74.
 Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.18% to 8,908.10.
 Hong Kong's  Hang Seng index  was up 1.53% in the last hour of trade on Friday, while mainland China's CSI 300 closed 1.39% lower at 3,985.50
 — Justina Lee 
 10 Hours Ago BP posts $8.5 billion third-quarter profit as oil prices soar
 A customer fills up a vehicle with fuel at a BP Plc petrol station in London, UK, on Monday, Aug. 4, 2025. Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images BP smashed third-quarter expectations on Friday, as volatile energy markets and high refining margins saw profits nearly quadruple year-on-year.
 The company reported $8.5 billion in underlying replacement cost profit, used as a proxy for net profit. That was above the $6.191 billion forecast by analysts in an LSEG-compiled consensus and up from $2.2 billion a year ago.
 Read more here . 
 — Jenni Reid 
 10 Hours Ago French economy unexpectedly shrank in third quarter
 Students carry out a blocking protest at the Cesar Baggio secondary school in Lille on September 29, 2026. Sameer Al-doumy | Afp | Getty Images France's economy contracted by 0.1% in the third quarter, flash data from statistics agency Insee showed on Friday. 
 Economists polled by Reuters had been expecting French gross domestic product to rise by 0.1% from the previous quarter. 
 In the second quarter, France's economy posted no growth. In the first quarter, GDP shrank by 0.2%. 
 Insee currently projects France will post annual GDP growth of 0.2% in 2026. 
 A decline in foreign trade dampened growth in the third quarter, with exports declining 1.7% following growth of 2.8% in the previous quarter. 
 "This decline was driven by a drop in exports of transport equipment (-9.1% after +20.8%), particularly in the aerospace sector," Insee said. 
 France is currently grappling with nationwide unrest , which began in Paris in late September. The government is also negotiating next year's budget with parliament, with an aim of slashing spending to bring down the country's deficit . 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 11 Hours Ago Futures point to mixed open in Europe
 Futures tied to European indexes pointed to a mixed open in Europe on Friday.
 Pan-European Stoxx 50 futures were down 0.5%, with futures tied to Germany's DAX index 0.2% lower ahead of the week's final opening bell. Futures tied to London's FTSE 100 and the French CAC 40 were up by around 0.2%, while those tied to Spain's IBEX 35 and the Italian FTSE MIB were flat. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 14 Hours Ago Biggest-ever crypto hack impacts $6.3 billion as Binance works to contain fallout
 Jakub Porzycki | Nurphoto | Getty Images Binance said Friday that a security incident had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, with around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets frozen so far, and pledged to cover all losses.
 The world's largest crypto exchange said an initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions."
 The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company funds, adding that customer funds remained safe.
 Binance also temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover funds.
 — Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio 
 14 Hours Ago BOJ holds rates as inflation aligns with 2% target for first time since 2013
 The Bank of Japan declared that inflation in the country was "generally consistent" with its target of 2%, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the target in 2013.
 This comes as the central bank expectedly held rates at 1.25%, still at its highest level since 1995.
 The decision was split 8-1, with board member Hajime Takata dissenting. Takata had wanted the bank to hike its policy rate to 1.5%.
 A CNBC survey of 16 economists before the decision revealed that all surveyed expect the BOJ to set the stage for a rate hike in December or January next year, as domestic inflation and wages continue to rise.
 Thirteen respondents said they expect a terminal rate, or the level at which the BOJ is expected to stop its tightening cycle, of 1.75% to 2% by around mid-2027.
 Japan has been grappling with a weak yen and high energy prices that have pushed up inflation.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 16 Hours Ago Mainland China shares fall over 1%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng gains 0.6%
 Mainland China and Hong Kong shares were mixed early Friday, tracking other Asian markets. 
 Hong Kong's  Hang Seng index  was up 0.55% , while mainland China's CSI 300 fell 1.21%. 
 The gains in Hang Seng were led by academic services and energy sectors, up nearly 4% and 1%, respectively. 
 — Justina Lee 
 16 Hours Ago Bitcoin tumbles below $78,000, extending losses as Binance security scare rattles crypto markets
 Nurphoto | Getty Images Bitcoin fell below $78,000 on Friday as concerns over a potential security breach at cryptocurrency exchange Binance rattled digital asset markets, prompting several major crypto firms to freeze billions of dollars in funds linked to the incident.
 The world's largest cryptocurrency fell over 4% to $77,994.96, extending its losses after breaking below the psychologically important $80,000 threshold.
 Ether , the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, dropped 4.84% to $2,247.45, while Binance's native token, BNB, tumbled 7.68% to $694.45.
 Defying the broader sell-off, Hyperliquid's HYPE token surged 9.7% to $89.08.
 Several cryptocurrency firms, including stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether, froze a combined $2.54 billion in funds linked to the suspected incident on Thursday.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 17 Hours Ago Asian tech stocks fall, tracking Wall Street losses 
 Asian technology stocks fell Friday, as overall lower-than-expected earnings of some U.S. tech firms and news of Binance's $5.7 billion crypto hack dented sentiment. 
 In Japan,  SoftBank Group  dropped 4.66%, while chip equipment maker  Tokyo Electron was 3.93% lower.  Advantest  lost 5.43%.
 In South Korea, SK Hynix fell 6.36%, while Samsung Electronics slipped 3.45%. 
 Tech stocks have been seeing heightened  volatility in recent sessions, with South Korea's semiconductor-heavy market whipsawing between steep losses and record gains.
 — Justina Lee 
 17 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets open mixed 
 Asia-Pacific markets traded mixed early Friday. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  slipped 0.68% while the Topix rose 0.26%.
 The Kospi dropped 3.11% at open, while the small-cap Kosdaq declined 2.35%. 
 Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.65% higher.
 — Justina Lee 
 18 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to open mixed 
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to open mixed Friday, as investors continue to assess the latest U.S. tech earnings while also keeping an eye on developments in the Middle East and the U.S. midterm elections. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  was poised to decline, with the Chicago futures contract at 63,775 and its Osaka counterpart last trading at 64,100, compared with the index's previous close of 64,659.47.
 Hong Kong  Hang Seng index  futures were at 23,108, compared with the index's last close of 22,958.65.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was trading 0.39% higher.
 Asia tech stocks may slip on Friday, after some major U.S. tech firms posted earnings that were below expectations. Google parent  Alphabet fell 12% Thursday after its adjusted earnings per share and revenue in the third quarter missed expectations. 
 — Justina Lee 
 19 Hours Ago Circle shares slide after company freezes funds affected by potential Binance 'security issue'
 Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) during the Circle Internet Financial Ltd. initial public offering (IPO) in New York, US, on Thursday, June 5, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Circle Internet Group said that the company froze more than 800 million in USD Coin associated with a potential security incident tied to cryptocurrency exchange Binance.
 In a social media post on Thursday, Binance said it was investigating "a potential security issue" on its trading platform.
 "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe. Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information."
 Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said Thursday evening that his company had frozen more than 800 million in USD Coin related to the incident. 
 Shares of Circle last traded down 4%.
 Read more here from CNBC's Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio on the potential security issue. 
 — Darla Mercado 
 19 Hours Ago These are the stocks making big moves in extended trading
 Several stocks made headlines in extended trading on Thursday evening as Amazon and Intel rolled out their latest results: 
 Amazon — Shares slid more than 6% after third-quarter results missed on the top and bottom lines. Amazon earned $1.89 per share on revenue of $201.94 billion, while analysts polled by LSEG sought $1.96 per share on $202.31 billion. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance for capital expenditures at $220 billion.
 Intel — The chipmaker tanked about 21% after guidance for the current quarter came in weaker than expected. Intel sees adjusted earnings of 25 cents per share on revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 43 cents and $17.1 billion in revenue, per LSEG.
 Sandisk — The data storage device manufacturer fell 3% even after reporting an earnings and revenue beat in its fiscal first-quarter financial report. It delivered adjusted earnings of $49.51 per share compared to analysts' estimates for $46.22, per LSEG. Sandisk also announced an eight-for-one forward stock split.
 Read more about Thursday's after-hours movers here .
 — Darla Mercado 
 19 Hours Ago Alphabet formed 'death cross' during Thursday slump 
 Alphabet, the parent of Google and YouTube that plunged nearly 13% Thursday, formed a "death cross" when the stock's 50-day moving average (roughly $340.26) crossed below its 200-day moving average (about $340.93).
 Alphabet last marked a " death cross " in July 2025. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Alphabet Class A shares in the past year — Scott Schnipper and Nick Wells 
 19 Hours Ago Nasdaq-100 futures fall as Amazon, Intel shares sell off after earnings
 Nasdaq-100 futures fell shortly after 6 p.m. in New York. 
 Nasdaq-100 futures lost 1.5%, while futures tied to the S&P 500 slid 0.6%. Dow futures added just 17 points.
 — Deena Zaidi
